prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: one achievement, targeted protein degradation, credited to Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The principle is simple enough to state in one sentence and is physically and chemically explicit: a small molecule enforces proximity between a chosen protein and an E3 ligase, ubiquitination follows, and the proteasome removes the target. That is a new capability, because inhibition is replaced by removal and previously undruggable proteins become reachable. It has been reproduced by many independent groups, is a standard acute-depletion tool, and has candidates in clinical trials. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the heterobifunctional PROTAC concept in 2001, and Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target in 2010 gave the molecular explanation that underpins the glue branch. Four colleagues independently converged on this trio or close to it, and the round-1 exchange removed my own Ciulli name for good reasons. I would write the citation around the shared mechanism, induced proximity to an E3 ligase, so that a non-specialist can follow it, with the two origins (concept and mechanism of an existing drug) stated in the scientific background.
statement.case_against: I still cannot dispose of three objections. First, no degrader is clearly approved as far as I know, so the clinical consequence is prospective and the prize could be early; this is from memory and I have not verified it against the record. Second, attribution is crowded and a three-name cap excludes Ciulli, Sakamoto, Ito, Kim and Gray, each of whom contributed something real, and the exclusion of Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures is a real cost. Third, PROTACs and cereblon glues were discovered by different groups at different times, so one citation risks joining two achievements; I accept that risk because the unifying mechanism is stronger than the historical separation, but a member who weighs the two as separate discoveries has a legitimate position.

responses.point: Aili would hold B027 for a later year because no degrader is approved and the Crews/Deshaies versus Handa split looks like two discoveries under one heading, whereas LNPs have already delivered clinically.
responses.response: The clinical point is fair and I do not dismiss it, but I do not think approval is the criterion; the committee has rewarded principles whose mechanism and independent reproduction were established before the products matured. On the two-discoveries objection, I would answer that induced proximity to an E3 ligase is the single principle, and Handa's cereblon work is what shows the same principle operating in a drug already in patients, so it is a confirmation as well as a separate finding. I also notice your own round-1 files concede that your Cullis, Madden and Hope trio omits the later optimisation and siRNA translation, so the attribution problem you raise against B027 is at least as severe for B062, where six names compete for three places. I keep B062 as my first alternative and would take it seriously in a later year once the credit is settled.

responses.point: Chabes supports B027 as a two-person part with Crews and Handa, paired with Liu's base editing, and accepts that dropping Deshaies is a real cost without a clean solution.
responses.response: We agree that Handa is indispensable, and I do not think a pairing is needed. I would not drop Deshaies, because he co-founded the PROTAC concept with Crews and a citation for the 2001 origin that omits him is hard to defend on priority. Since we have three places for one achievement, there is no pressure to cut him. I also doubt that adding base editing as a second part strengthens the case: Liu alone is clean, but with the 2020 CRISPR prize and a short clinical record it is a judgement about timing that is separate from B027. I would ask whether you could support Crews, Deshaies and Handa as a sole part, since that is the arrangement that comes nearest to five votes.

responses.point: Sparr asked how I would handle Handa and the cereblon work without overcrowding three names, and doubts that the PROTAC and glue branches can be one citation.
responses.response: My answer is that Handa is already inside the trio. Having moved from Ciulli to Handa, the three names are Crews and Deshaies for the concept and demonstration of PROTACs, and Handa for the cereblon mechanism that explains glue degraders, so there is no overcrowding. The citation is then written on the shared principle of recruiting an E3 ligase, which is chemistry in the sense you apply to lipids: a defined molecular interaction that is designed and measured. I accept your point that the clinical proof is outstanding, and I accept that your lipid work is the strongest present-day clinical case on the list; our difference is whether a mature principle with a still-pending clinical record can be recognised, and I think it can.

responses.point: Aqvist agrees on the ranking, argues that Handa's cereblon identification is an independent mechanistic discovery rather than a refinement, and names Ciulli as the strongest fourth name.
responses.response: I accept your argument and Brzezinski's, and it is why Handa now stands in my trio in place of Ciulli. Your remark that VHL-based degrader work refines a concept Crews and Deshaies had already shown helps me hold that line against the cost of omitting Ciulli, which I still regard as the most visible hole. I would put on record that the committee should state in the background document why Ciulli, Sakamoto and Ito fall outside the three, so the choice reads as a priority judgement and not an oversight.

uncertainties: Clinical status of degraders (whether any is approved, and the strength of late-stage data) is from memory and unverified; if the record is weaker than I believe, the case for early recognition weakens.
Whether one citation honestly spans PROTACs and cereblon glues, or whether that joins two discoveries by different groups at different times.
Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Sakamoto and Ito is contestable and Ciulli is the most notable omission.
Whether a configuration can reach five votes, given that Aili and Sparr prefer B062, and Chabes, Somfai and Zou prefer other achievements.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. I am a Lund nanophysicist whose work on molecular motors and nanowire devices does not tie to any nominee. Lund colleagues Somfai and Sparr sit on the committee, and I see no personal or institutional link to the credited people. As chair and a physicist I weigh mechanism and generative potential heavily, and that may shape my view of B027 and I have said so openly.
